A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same B-spline neural PDE framework. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite renaming and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE-learning experiments, prediction errors, training times, and ablations, including additional experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original PDE-learning results, an expanded recovery-probability comparison, retained ablations, and an additional annular-surface reconstruction experiment.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix C.2 adds an auxiliary geometric reconstruction procedure using separate B-splines for x, y, and z, with boundary fitting followed by interior least squares. The central coefficient-network PDE solver remains unchanged; renaming PI-DBSN to PI-BSNet and explicitly separating boundary losses mainly clarify the existing framework.

E1.justification: Recovery probability, Burgers, advection, trapezoid diffusion, and 3D heat studies are retained across the main text and appendices. v2 adds an annular-surface fitting example in Appendix C.2, extending domain and task coverage without demonstrating PDE learning on the annulus.

E2.justification: The recovery comparison expands from PINN and PI-DeepONet to include EPINN, SFHCPINN, HWPINN, VS-PINN, CAN-PINN, and PI-FNO. These methods have reported results in v2 Figures 2–4 and 10. The PINN comparison for 3D heat is retained.

E3.justification: Recovery-comparison PINN and PI-DeepONet activations change from ReLU to Tanh, and v2 uses RTX 4090 timing instead of v1's CPU/A100 presentations. Figure 4 reports average L2 error rather than the earlier MSE. Separately, v2 Section 5.3 states 10 trapezoid training parameters while Appendix D.3 retains 50, leaving that sample-count revision unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds a finite-difference PI-BSNet training variant, an explicit ICBC-loss analysis, and the annulus reconstruction case study. The standalone A100 experiment is removed. Derivative checks, control-point optimality, control-count sensitivity, noise/loss-weight tests, and network-depth ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies Figure 3 as mean and standard deviation over 10 independent runs and Figure 4 as ten-run averages. v1 already specifies ten-run statistics for ablations but does not identify the main comparison this way. An increase in the number of runs is not established.

E6.justification: v2 supplies new recovery-comparison results for additional baselines and the finite-difference variant under revised settings, plus annulus reconstruction results. The A100 timing table and 3D heat training residual are omitted. Other PDE aggregate errors and all four retained ablation tables remain unchanged; heat testing residuals remain 0.0121 for PINN and 0.0032 for the proposed method.

T1.justification: The broadly stated generalization result in v1 Appendix B.2 becomes explicitly restricted to elliptic/parabolic PDEs in v2 Theorem 4.6. v2 also defines domain regularity, revises proof norm estimates and approximation quantifiers, and adds a full-rank least-squares condition. The displayed advection equation changes from s_t + u s s_x = 0 to s_t + u s_x = 0.

C1.justification: The family-learning and universal-approximation contributions remain. v2 explicitly qualifies the generalization guarantee as covering elliptic/parabolic families and emphasizes efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs, nonhomogeneous ICBCs, and nonrectangular domains. The earlier emphasis on 3D dynamics recedes, although that experiment remains in the appendix.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial discussion of fixed versus learned basis expressiveness, suitability for smooth solutions and strict ICBC requirements, control-point selection, and separate dimensionality costs for sampling and network size. It also distinguishes general-domain surface representation from future PDE learning there, extending v1's shorter dimensionality and geometry limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds training pseudocode, detailed baseline implementations, advection data-generation instructions, and the trapezoid solver's forward-Euler step and spatial resolution. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, v1's explicit evaluation meshes and the 3D PINN's training-epoch and loss-weight specifications are omitted.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand positioning against hard-constraint PINNs, efficient PINNs, and parametric learning methods, including Wang et al. (2023), Chiu et al. (2022), and Ko and Park (2025). v2 also adds theoretical and scalability references and removes the earlier justification for excluding FNO from experiments.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Supporting theory moves into reorganized appendices, advection and trapezoid studies move into the main text, and 3D heat moves out. A separate discussion section and contents listing are added, alongside title, author, and method-name changes.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Recovery heatmaps become extensive surface/error panels, loss plots are reorganized, and a timing–error scatterplot replaces the main timing table. New basis and annulus figures are added; existing heat comparisons are merged and trapezoid panels rearranged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's limited recovery comparison, v2 directly tests relevant hard-constraint and efficiency-oriented baselines, adds a finite-difference control, and explicitly reports ten-run summaries. These strengthen the empirical support, while expanded discussion clarifies applicability. The net improvement is limited by unclear MSE-versus-L2 reporting, conflicting trapezoid training counts, and removal of some evaluation and training details.
